author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The New England Patriots have placed wide receiver A.J. Brown on injured reserve after he sustained a high ankle sprain in his debut with the team. The roster move means Brown must miss at least four games, turning what had been a week-to-week injury question into a defined early-season absence.

Brown left the game in the third quarter and did not return. High ankle sprains can limit a receiver’s acceleration, cutting and ability to absorb contact, making recovery timelines particularly important for a player expected to carry a large share of the passing game. The injured-reserve designation gives Brown additional time to rehabilitate without occupying an active roster spot.

New England will now have to redistribute targets and snaps while its new star receiver is unavailable. The four-game minimum does not guarantee Brown will return as soon as he is eligible; his progress will determine when the team activates him. The transaction is a significant change from the immediate uncertainty after the injury and gives the Patriots a clearer planning window for the next portion of their schedule.
dek: The high ankle sprain suffered in Brown’s Patriots debut will sideline the star receiver for at least four games.
headline: Patriots place A.J. Brown on injured reserve
